verdict.rationale: GitCafe's own webhook docs say a webhook sends a signed HTTPS request to your server when something happens in a repository or organization, such as a push, a new issue or a merged pull request. That is a real outbound HTTP callback a programmatic consumer can subscribe to and receive. The evidence is a single doc line, though, so the depth is unverified. Missing for 10: full event catalogue, how webhooks are registered or managed (UI/API/CLI), signature verification and retry/delivery-log details, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
